page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.24xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with an AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, providing 96 dedicated physical cores across 96 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Memory allocation totals 768 GB, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. High-density storage is integrated directly via 60,000 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, backed by a 150 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance contains no hardware accelerators or GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate extreme throughput across parallel processing and memory operations. While single-core results remain in the middle tier—yielding 1,705.99 in stress-ng and 1,884.0 in Geekbench—the 96 non-hyperthreaded cores excel in parallel execution, reaching a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 26,370.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 918.05 GB/sec. Memory subsystems register exceptional bandwidth, recording 480.71 GB/sec on large read blocks and 217.63 GB/sec on large write blocks.

Data-intensive operational tests demonstrate top-tier performance characteristics. PassMark database operations reached 47,386.36, and Redis SET throughput recorded 195.85 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput also measured in the top tier at 124.71 GB/sec. Tradeoffs center on per-thread single-core execution speed and the architectural requirement for arm64 software support, as x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 are absent.

Given the dense 60 TB local NVMe array, 768 GB memory footprint, and massive network capacity, the i8ge.24xlarge delivers strong qualitative resource efficiency for scaled architectures. The instance is suited for high-throughput distributed databases, large-scale Redis in-memory caches, big data analytics engines, and write-heavy data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8ge.24xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System, featuring a 96-core AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 2.8 GHz with dedicated physical cores. It provides 768 GB of memory, paired with 60,000 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 150 Gbps baseline networking. Without GPUs, its performance profile emphasizes multi-threaded and memory-bound throughput. In benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in multi-core processing, sustained memory bandwidth exceeding 480 GB/sec on reads, and over 195 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution sits in the median range and requires arm64 application compatibility, the generous 8 GB per core memory ratio and local NVMe density offer significant efficiency for scale-up operations. It is designed for large-scale distributed databases, extensive in-memory caching clusters, high-volume real-time data streaming, and analytics workloads.
